title: Yesterday’s scraps, today’s rejected fritters
odia:
ଖୁଣ୍ଟି ଖାଉଥିଲୁ ମଦରଙ୍ଗା ଶାଗ
ପିଠି ଖାଉଥିଲା ଖରା
କାଲି ଚାଟୁଥିଲୁ ଅଇଁଠା ପତର
ଆଜି ରୁଚୁ ନାହିଁ ବରା।
literal_meaning: You used to pick and eat madaranga greens; your back took the sun. Yesterday you licked a used eating leaf; today fritters do not please your taste.
meaning_odia: ଆଗେ ମଦରଙ୍ଗା ଶାଗ ଖୁଣ୍ଟି ଖାଇବା, ଖରାରେ ପିଠି ରହିବା ଓ ଅଇଁଠା ପତର ଚାଟିବାର କଥା ମନେ ପକାଇ ବକ୍ତା ଆଜି ବରା ନରୁଚିବାକୁ ଟାହି କରୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଅବସ୍ଥା ବଦଳିବା ସହ ରୁଚି ଓ ଆଚରଣ ବଦଳିଯିବା ପ୍ରତି ଏହି ଆକ୍ଷେପ; ଅଭାବରେ ଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ହେୟ କରିବା ଏହାର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: The speaker sets remembered hardship against a newly fastidious appetite. Greens, sun on the back and scraps on an eating leaf build the first picture; rejected fritters provide the sharp reversal. Our editorial reading hears a taunt that the addressee has forgotten earlier circumstances. The contempt in that accusation belongs to the speaker.
usage_example: Original imagined example: In a discussion of the verse, a reader notices how yesterday and today compress a change in circumstances. Another points out that the taunt reveals the speaker’s resentment as well as the addressee’s changed taste.
cultural_context: The word for eating recurs in the image of the back taking the sun, linking hunger with exposure. The final contrast moves from licking remnants to finding fritters unappealing. Its force comes from the speaker’s pointed arrangement of those images.

odia_summary: ଆଗର ଅଭାବ ସହ ଆଜିର ବାଛବିଚାରକୁ ତୁଳନା କରି ବକ୍ତାର ଟାହି।
english_summary: A speaker taunts changed tastes by recalling earlier hardship.
